evidence: performance-logging.module.ts: @Module({ providers: [PerformanceLoggingInterceptor, PerformanceLoggingService], exports: [...] }): the module supplies the service through Nest dependency injection
performance-logging.interceptor.ts: PerformanceLoggingInterceptor receives the service via its constructor, `private readonly performanceLoggingService: PerformanceLoggingService`
performance-logging.interceptor.ts: LogPerformance creates its own copy with `const performanceLoggingService = new PerformanceLoggingService();`, bypassing the module's provider

performance-logging.interceptor.ts: the timing and logging steps (startTime = performance.now(); logPerformance({ className, methodName, startTime })) appear three times: once in intercept and in both the Promise and sync branches of LogPerformance
Most importers of the interceptor file (four services and portfolio-calculator.ts) are not the module, so most callers likely use the bypassing decorator
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with one concern, performance logging, but they don't use the module's own way of supplying the logging service consistently. PerformanceLoggingModule registers and exports PerformanceLoggingInterceptor and PerformanceLoggingService through Nest dependency injection, and the interceptor gets the service through its constructor. The LogPerformance decorator in the same file instead creates its own copy with `new PerformanceLoggingService()` on every call, so it never uses the module's instance. Any configuration or dependencies the module's copy gets won't reach decorated methods. The decorator is exported from this file, and five of its seven importers are not the module (four services and portfolio-calculator.ts), so the bypass is used widely. The timing and logging steps (startTime via performance.now(), then logPerformance with className, methodName and startTime) are also written out three times: once in intercept and twice in LogPerformance, in separate async and sync branches. There is no shared helper. A Nest decorator can't easily use the module's providers, so this is partly a practical workaround, which keeps confidence moderate. Under this rubric it still counts as bypassing the module's abstractions and duplicating its logic.

violations.message: The LogPerformance decorator creates its own PerformanceLoggingService with `new PerformanceLoggingService()` on each call instead of using the instance PerformanceLoggingModule provides, which PerformanceLoggingInterceptor gets through its constructor. The file therefore uses two different ways to get the service.

The timing and logging steps (performance.now() for startTime, then logPerformance({ className, methodName, startTime })) are repeated in intercept and in both the async and sync branches of LogPerformance. They should be moved into one shared helper.
